report:
PASS for the requested new100 partial packet, with the harmless Lemma 2 clarification specified below. This verdict does not resolve original P21.3.

I checked the argument independently, including the supplied primary proofs and their applicability, and opened the cited CLD v2 source. The nine premise records below contain external mathematical statements, without the packet’s reading claims, hashes, acceptance history, or proof commentary. No earlier strict-PL theorem, curve theorem, predecessor packet, or supporting note is used as a grant.

Lemma 1 is valid. Competing positive-test decompositions determine identical signed measures because they agree against compact smooth scalars and these are dense among compact continuous scalars. Applying density inside the complement of the test’s support establishes the intrinsic support assertion. Symmetric projection handles the remaining tests. On a compact moment presentation, Θ^q has signed coefficient matrix q! times the identity in orthonormal exterior coordinates. Its restriction remains positive definite on every tangent space of dimension at least q; on smaller faces the relevant restrictions vanish. Finitely many faces therefore give the required common domination constant. The compact analytic neighborhood can contain the cutoff support in its ordinary interior, so the inequalities suffice wherever the cutoff is nonzero. Measure domination then proves C⁰ continuity in the actual chart topology. Restriction and independence of finite positive-current decompositions follow from coefficient-measure uniqueness.

The two limit arguments are correctly separated. Decreasing sequences use finite coefficient measures of one fixed current and common compact bounds. Continuous multiplication on varying positive nets uses smooth scalar approximation and eventual, rather than global, bounds on each tested mass. No discontinuous multiplier is passed through a varying-current limit.

Lemma 2’s sentence ‘The limit is positive’ must mean that S is positive. The precise statement is: S is positive, and v_a S_a converges weakly to vS when the continuous v_a converge locally uniformly to v; positivity of the multiplied limit is guaranteed when v is nonnegative. For a nonzero positive S and v=-1, vS=-S is not positive. This is a wording clarification, not a substantive repair: the proof establishes positivity of S, and no subsequent inference uses positivity of a product with an arbitrary signed continuous scalar. Positivity of differentiated generated-potential products is established separately by Theorem 1. The frozen paper has not been edited.

The sheafified transfinite construction is sound. Each membership condition is ordinary-local, the stages increase, and their sections remain upper semicontinuous. The set of all open/section pairs bounds the number of strict increases; an equal-successor stage is fixed under both the successor operation and subsequent sheafified limit operations. Minimality then identifies the stationary sheaf with generated Psh. At a successor with locally bounded real final u, every predecessor is finite because u_j≥u and +∞ is excluded. Upper semicontinuity bounds u_1 above on compact sets, while u bounds all predecessors below. Thus every predecessor qualifies for induction and the common bounds in (9) are justified. Both equations d′D(uT)=0 and d″D(uT)=0 follow from square-zero and anticommutation. The endpoint degrees and the ordered recursion through top degree are valid.

Theorem 2’s smooth base case follows from smooth multiplication, differential duality, and the smooth-factor identity. At successors its left side uses the fixed positive current D(vT); its right side uses varying positive D(u_jT) with the continuous multiplier v. Limit ranks and localization are legitimate. Adjacent interchanges therefore establish permutation independence with at most one discontinuous factor, including the maximal permitted number of factors. Signed coefficient measures also justify the subtraction in Corollary 2.2.

Theorem 3 has the correct orientation. On each subopen, take the potentially discontinuous differentiating potential as u and U or V as the continuous factor in Theorem 2. Compatibility identifies the positive currents D(US) and D(VS), whose Borel products with the same locally bounded potential consequently agree. Addition, scaling, ordinary restriction, compatible sheaf gluing, fixed-degree weak positive limits, and smooth middle-positive doubly closed decorations preserve the stated property. For a decoration of type (r,r), the output degree restriction is p+r≤n−1. No arbitrary-current density assertion is needed or obtained.

The external hypotheses apply on the original ordinary opens over either valuation regime. Compact-support localization requires no global paracompactness. Canonical integration and generic component lengths are retained throughout, including singular and nonreduced spaces. The packet does not depend on reverse Psh/CPsh recognition or on the broader strongly-positive spanning inference. CLD 8.5.3’s indexing inconsistency is bypassed by the correctly graded smooth identity and its duality proof. The false dimension-equality clause in CLD 12.2.4 is excluded; its needed polyhedrality assertion is independently corroborated by the cited [Ducros theorem 3.2](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~antoine.ducros/tropicbis.pdf), whose bound is dimension at most that of the source. The displayed primary closure and symmetry proofs do not justify discontinuous extensions by uniform closure alone; the packet supplies its own transfinite arguments. In particular, unrestricted continuous scalar multiplication is not a closed-current closure, and the printed CLD 8.6.7 assertion is not adopted.

Proposition 4 is correct: commutation evaluated at zero implies invariance of the measure under each shear. Compact invariant support forces first y=0 and then x=0. The displayed Laurent maps and their inverses are analytic torus automorphisms inducing exactly those shears. The diagnostic surface has the required ambient properties; strict polyannulus neighborhoods can be chosen with radii powers of 2. The partition-of-unity calculation correctly exhibits failure of closedness without overlap compatibility. Neither diagnostic supplies an admissible analytic counterexample.

Finally, the two-sign sufficient condition and the proposed exhaustion implication are valid under their explicit antecedents. Neither antecedent is established for arbitrary currents or equal-curvature differences. Mixed symmetry still contains D(hT), and D[h]=0 only identifies its canonical-integration counterpart. The requested partial results are established; original P21.3 remains unresolved by this packet.

passages.statement: CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, §11.1, 11.1.7, 15.7.1–2 and 15.2.2–9: The ground field is complete non-Archimedean and may be trivially valued. Analytic spaces have bases of compact neighborhoods, good analytic spaces have bases of affinoid neighborhoods, and ordinary opens are analytic domains. A topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space has its canonical calibrated level-n tropical structure, compatible with analytic-domain restriction. A good Hausdorff analytic space is locally holomorphically separated, and a locally holomorphically separated analytic space is locally differentially separated. On a locally holomorphically separated analytic space, compact sets admit compactly supported smooth cutoffs inside prescribed ordinary neighborhoods; compactly supported continuous real functions admit uniform approximation by compactly supported smooth functions inside prescribed ordinary open neighborhoods of their supports, retaining prescribed constant lower and upper bounds. An ordinary open cover of a compact set admits finite nonnegative compactly supported smooth localization subordinate to that cover, with sum equal to one near the compact set.

passages.statement: CLD v2, Definitions 8.1.1 and 8.1.7 and Lemma 8.1.4: On an affined G-tropical space, generated Psh is the smallest ordinary subsheaf of functions with values in R∪{−∞} containing smooth functions with positive smooth Hessian and closed under decreasing sequential limits. Its ordinal construction starts with those smooth generators, takes ordinary-local decreasing sequential limits at successors, and ordinary-local membership in earlier stages at limit ordinals. CPsh is instead the smallest ordinary subsheaf of real continuous functions containing the same smooth generators and closed under uniform sequential limits.

passages.statement: CLD v2, Proposition 6.5.2, Definition 7.2.1, Remark 7.2.3, Lemmas 7.2.4 and 7.2.7(b), and Propositions 1.2.12, 1.10.3 and 3.5.5: Every compactly supported symmetric smooth (q,q)-form whose support is contained in a paracompact locally differentially separated open is a difference of two compactly supported middle-positive smooth forms; the support condition holds for compact supports on almost-good analytic spaces. On a locally differentially separated level-n tropical space, middle-positive currents are symmetric and nonnegative on middle-positive complementary compact tests, and middle positivity is ordinary-local. The middle-positive current cone is pointed. Wedges of middle-positive forms are middle-positive, and wedging a middle-positive current with a smooth middle-positive form preserves middle positivity in compatible degrees.

passages.statement: CLD v2, Proposition 7.2.8 and §7.2.11: On a locally differentially separated level-n tropical space, positive Radon measures correspond bijectively to positive scalar-test currents, and their induced currents have order zero. For a middle-positive current T and a middle-positive complementary smooth form η, T∧η corresponds to a unique positive Radon measure μ satisfying ∫g dμ=⟨T,gη⟩ for every compactly supported smooth scalar g. This coefficient measure has compact support when η does.
passages.quote:
Proposition 7.2.8. — Soit X un espace tropical de niveau n, localement différentiel-
lement séparé.
  a) Toute mesure de Radon positive µ sur X induit, par restriction à Ac (X), un courant
positif [µ] d’ordre 0.
  b) L’application µ 7→ [µ] ainsi définie est une bijection continue de l’espace des me-
sures de Radon positives sur X sur l’espace des courants positifs de bidimension (0, 0)

passages.statement: CLD v2, Proposition 7.2.8 and §7.2.11: On a locally differentially separated level-n tropical space, positive Radon measures correspond bijectively to positive scalar-test currents, and their induced currents have order zero. For a middle-positive current T and a middle-positive complementary smooth form η, T∧η corresponds to a unique positive Radon measure μ satisfying ∫g dμ=⟨T,gη⟩ for every compactly supported smooth scalar g. This coefficient measure has compact support when η does.
passages.quote:
Le courant T ∧ω est positif, de bidimension (0, 0) ; d’après la proposition 7.2.8,
il est donc associé à une unique mesure µTω sur X. Cette mesure applique une fonction
lisse à suppport compact u sur ⟨uT, ω⟩. Lorsque ω est à support compact, cette mesure
est à support compact.

passages.statement: CLD v2, §§1.2.6–7, Definition 1.10.1, §§3.3.1–2, Theorem 12.2.4 and §§7.1.1–3: For a symmetric (q,q)-superform written as σ_q Σ a_IJ d′x_I∧d″x_J, where σ_q=(−1)^{q(q−1)/2}, middle positivity is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of the symmetric matrix (a_IJ) on the qth exterior power. Positivity on a polyhedral space is tested on tangent spaces of cells, and it suffices to test maximal cells of a cellular decomposition. The tropical image of a compact analytic space under a moment map is compact polyhedral. Compactly supported test-form topology is the inductive topology over fixed compact supports and covering moment presentations, with cellwise coefficient C^r seminorms. On a locally differentially separated space, continuity may be checked on fixed ordinary moment charts after multiplication by nonnegative compactly supported smooth cutoffs. premises: CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, §11.1, 11.1.7, 15.7.1–2 and 15.2.2–9: The ground field is complete non-Archimedean and may be trivially valued. Analytic spaces have bases of compact neighborhoods, good analytic spaces have bases of affinoid neighborhoods, and ordinary opens are analytic domains. A topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space has its canonical calibrated level-n tropical structure, compatible with analytic-domain restriction. A good Hausdorff analytic space is locally holomorphically separated, and a locally holomorphically separated analytic space is locally differentially separated. On a locally holomorphically separated analytic space, compact sets admit compactly supported smooth cutoffs inside prescribed ordinary neighborhoods; compactly supported continuous real functions admit uniform approximation by compactly supported smooth functions inside prescribed ordinary open neighborhoods of their supports, retaining prescribed constant lower and upper bounds. An ordinary open cover of a compact set admits finite nonnegative compactly supported smooth localization subordinate to that cover, with sum equal to one near the compact set.

CLD v2, Definitions 8.1.1 and 8.1.7 and Lemma 8.1.4: On an affined G-tropical space, generated Psh is the smallest ordinary subsheaf of functions with values in R∪{−∞} containing smooth functions with positive smooth Hessian and closed under decreasing sequential limits. Its ordinal construction starts with those smooth generators, takes ordinary-local decreasing sequential limits at successors, and ordinary-local membership in earlier stages at limit ordinals. CPsh is instead the smallest ordinary subsheaf of real continuous functions containing the same smooth generators and closed under uniform sequential limits.

CLD v2, Proposition 6.5.2, Definition 7.2.1, Remark 7.2.3, Lemmas 7.2.4 and 7.2.7(b), and Propositions 1.2.12, 1.10.3 and 3.5.5: Every compactly supported symmetric smooth (q,q)-form whose support is contained in a paracompact locally differentially separated open is a difference of two compactly supported middle-positive smooth forms; the support condition holds for compact supports on almost-good analytic spaces. On a locally differentially separated level-n tropical space, middle-positive currents are symmetric and nonnegative on middle-positive complementary compact tests, and middle positivity is ordinary-local. The middle-positive current cone is pointed. Wedges of middle-positive forms are middle-positive, and wedging a middle-positive current with a smooth middle-positive form preserves middle positivity in compatible degrees.

CLD v2, Proposition 7.2.8 and §7.2.11: On a locally differentially separated level-n tropical space, positive Radon measures correspond bijectively to positive scalar-test currents, and their induced currents have order zero. This coefficient measure has compact support when η does.
